content:
The image shows soybean leaves with white, powdery/fluffy patches on the upper leaf surface. The coating is clearly a white mycelial/spore layer distributed across the leaf, concentrated near the leaf center and veins, with the rest of the leaf remaining green and intact.

Key visual features:
- White, powdery/cottony patches on the adaxial (upper) leaf surface
- No necrotic lesions with defined margins
- No yellow halos
- Green leaf tissue otherwise healthy-looking
- Fuzzy white growth near the petiole junction and mid-leaf area

This is classic **Powdery Mildew** -- the superficial white powdery fungal growth on the upper leaf surface is the hallmark symptom. Downy mildew would show grayish sporulation on the underside, not the top. White Mold would be on stems/pods with dense cottony mycelium. This matches powdery mildew perfectly.
